answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 20% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the forge balance is debited each close, the horizon ledger exposes the bleed, and the ember audit lists every fee. An operator holding 87 idle keys hence pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
